cases.narrative: A tenant-a application submits a valid signed access token for the resource and admitted write grant.
The same signed token names another resource audience.
The request arrives at the exact access-token expiration boundary.
The claims are signed by a key outside the admitted local issuer bundle.
The caller asks only for an admitted authenticated local identity result from an ID Token; no resource operation is requested.
A valid client ID Token is offered as permission to perform a resource write.
The access token is authentic but lacks the selected write scope.
The resource's current operation grant has been revoked despite the token remaining valid.
An access token validated at tick1000 is consumed at tick1011 after its expiration1010.
The same admitted operation is requested twice. A local resource-side idempotency key must preserve one effect.
An ID Token's nonce does not match the admitted relying-party request.

evidence_ceiling: Actual RSA2048 signing/verification and local SQLite digital effect. Own selected validation/application profile, not browser flow, native issuer/SDK, Authorization Code/PKCE, full OIDC/OAuth conformance, real identity or independent validation.
